premises.text: Overheating limits compute performance and reliability as data demand outpaces cooling
premises.evidence_span: The more you ask your computer to do stuff, it overheats. And as it overheats, it becomes slower

premises.text: Proprietary two-phase cooling reaches CPU temperatures no market cooling system can (demo ~13°C)
premises.evidence_span: It says 13 degrees Celsius. That's around 30 degrees Fahrenheit, I think, in the US. That is the lowest temperature you can ever get on the CPU. No system in the world can do that

premises.text: Solution ships as a standard drop-in server with integrated cooling
premises.evidence_span: It's a standard server. You can insert it in any data center today, so you don't have to change a thing

premises.text: Going low on CPU temperature yields both higher speed and better energy efficiency
premises.evidence_span: By going lower on the CPU, we both accelerate it, so we make it go faster, and we can actually make it more energy efficient

value.text: Cool servers to accelerate innovation with the fastest, most efficient compute
value.evidence_span: world's fastest and most efficient server to accelerate your innovation
